analysis:
The PR changes docs/architecture/inference.md only: the "Last updated" date, and the Nemotron Super media body cap, which goes from 8 MiB to 40 MiB (patch hunks at base 128-130 and 540-541, head 128-132 and 542-544). The supplied units are base text at lines 802-1609 and do not include the changed hunks. I reviewed them as surrounding context and relied on the patch excerpt for the changed lines. No runtime code is in the supplied evidence.

Relevant surfaces are TB-002 and TB-007. The documented change raises the encoded-body ceiling to hold one part at the shared 25 MiB inline-media cap as base64, and the over-cap response becomes `media_too_large`. The memory charge is still taken from the shared budget before decoding (503 on failure), and the owner lock, the per-owner limit of one image request at a time (429 on a second), and the context checks remain. This implies a small increase in pre-admission memory and availability exposure, in the T-010/T-029 DoS class. The evidence does not show that the code diverges from the documentation or that admission accounting is bypassed.

The unchanged base context was checked against the threat model. It covers GLM media handling, prefix-cache exclusion for media (T-041 unaffected), calibration, deadlines and MTP. None of it alters crypto, attestation or authorization, or the cache-scope assumptions.

Open question for integration: whether the code change behind this doc edit (the NemotronSuperServingPolicy.maximumEncodedBodyBytes constant and the transport body limits) still charges the media memory reservation before decoding. That code is not in the supplied batch, so I recorded it as an unverified contract rather than a finding.
